content: Discussion thread for #Project announcements > leanprover-community/intentions

With this consolidation, it may be a good time to consider further features, for interested projects to try it out, and may even for us to start thinking about how to build a "federated" cross-repository mechanism for reporting/discovering intentions to work on formalization topics -- so far this is solely within individual repositories.

Could this support tasks which might take more than one PR to complete? (an unknown number of PRs/parts)

Maybe with a variant of propose that only says "this is partial progress towards the goal" and when the PR is merged the state will go back to "claimed" rather than "completed".
Also, do you plan to add this to Mathlib? (I'm wondering how would I claim a problem from 1000.yaml for example)

Snir Broshi said:

Could this support tasks which might take more than one PR to complete? (an unknown number of PRs/parts)

Maybe with a variant of propose that only says "this is partial progress towards the goal" and when the PR is merged the state will go back to "claimed" rather than "completed".

I'm not sure that there's much additional value here, over just mentioning the issue in the PR, or vice versa.

Snir Broshi said:

Also, do you plan to add this to Mathlib? (I'm wondering how would I claim a problem from 1000.yaml for example)

That's a question for the mathlib maintainers. :-)

I think there are a number of things we would need, first:

  1. Clear explanation that the intention registration system is optional, and if someone ignores it and PRs something you'd registered, they can just say "oops?" and move on.
  2. A mechanism for dismissing registrations, if maintainers/reviewers don't think the claim is credible, think it is for too long a duration, or that the claimer has made too many claims.
  3. ... hmmm, maybe actually not much else, perhaps we should try this!

Then how about non-exclusive claims? Just to signal to the community "I'm on it, casually".
OTOH this means opening issues, which in turn means more PR spam from bad faith LLM users, so maybe this is not worth it.
@Snir Broshi : in that situation (split PRs) I would propose creating sub issues.
I think "I'm on it, casually", is probably a signal to be discouraged. :-)

Kim Morrison said:

I think "I'm on it, casually", is probably a signal to be discouraged. :-)

I disagree. At worst it should be ignored, but not discouraged. Discouraging this may also discourage people from getting into lean, since doing a project casually is a common avenue for this.
Of course, it's great that people work on projects casually, but then there's no need to tell others about it, is there?
Personally I would love to know what others are working on casually, and it'll affect what I choose to work on, both to suggest collabs and to avoid stepping on others

Having two people casually interested in related material - not necessarily the same results, but things that might plausibly end up wanting to use some of the same definitions and associated API - is enough basis for each of them to start PRing their definitions and API to mathlib sooner than they might otherwise, so they can benefit from each other's work where applicable, for example.

Yes, I agree now that "casual" intentions should be in scope.

The leanprover-community/intentions mechanism includes an upgrade over previous versions in that it also collects any free-form text following the claim command. I suggest that for now this is sufficient (and we should remind people to use it!) so that people can say there "lol, just thinking about it" or "omg, this is my BSc thesis project, please don't touch".

Following @Emily Riehl's and @María Inés de Frutos Fernández 's suggestions we ended up with some infrastructure that hopefully will help in keeping track of ongoing formalization projects in Lean, in particular relying on Mathlib (but not only) using the Intentions repository. This is documented in our community webpage and it is hosted at this repository, whose main page contains instructions about how to add projects and about the aims and scope of the infrastructure.

Basically, projects can be visualized and searched on this page of the aforementioned repository. As you might see there, they're classified according to their status (Planned, In Progress, In Review, Completed, Abandoned). Once a project is registered there, an automatic message is triggered on the Zulip channel #Project intentions where users are not meant to post anything.
